content.title: About
content.content: Almond butter is a paste made by grinding whole almonds into a smooth, spreadable consistency. It has a mild nutty flavor, creamy texture, and is used as an alternative to butter or other nut spreads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Almond butter retains nearly all the nutrients found in whole almonds, but in a more concentrated form.
Unlike peanut butter, almond butter is free of peanuts and is suitable for people with peanut allergies.
It is a popular ingredient in vegan cooking as a butter substitute.
There are two main varieties: smooth and crunchy, the latter containing small almond pieces.
Almond butter can be kept at room temperature for up to 6 months, but lasts longer when refrigerated.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Monounsaturated fats support heart health and help regulate cholesterol levels.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: Protein and fiber promote satiety and support digestive health.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium is essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: People with nut allergies may experience reactions, up to anaphylaxis, from almond butter.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Almond butter is calorie-dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Oxalates can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread almond butter on toast, stir it into smoothies, sauces, baked goods, oatmeal, or yogurt. It also serves as a base for dressings and dessert creams.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store almond butter in a sealed jar in a cool, dark place. For longer shelf life keep it refrigerated, where it stays fresh for up to a year. Discard if it develops a rancid smell or changes color.

barbecue-beef-sandwich-on-white-bun.title: Barbecue Beef Sandwich on White Bun

content.title: About
content.content: The Barbecue Beef Sandwich features a juicy slice of beef marinated in smoky barbecue sauce, grilled to a golden crust, and served on a soft white bun. It combines the rich flavor of the sauce, a hint of sweetness from tomatoes, and the light crunch of the bun.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sandwich originated in the United States in the 1970s as part of fast‑food menus.
Traditional barbecue sauce is made from tomato paste, vinegar, brown sugar, and spices such as paprika and garlic.
The white bun is often toasted on the grill to add a slight crust and prevent sogginess from the sauce.
Beef used in the sandwich typically comes from the sirloin or shoulder, providing a balance of tenderness and flavor.
Some regions add pickles or sauerkraut for an extra flavor contrast.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef is an excellent source of complete protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat provides easily absorbed heme iron, supporting healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef supplies B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: The sandwich fits moderate low‑carb diets when a whole‑grain bun is chosen.

items.title: Antioxidants in the sauce
items.content: Tomatoes and spices in barbecue sauce contain lycopene and polyphenols with antioxidant properties.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Large portions of beef can raise cholesterol levels, so moderation is recommended.

items.title: Sodium in the sauce
items.content: Barbecue sauce often contains a lot of salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The white bun usually contains wheat; those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity need a gluten‑free alternative.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: The sandwich can be calorie‑rich due to meat, sauce, and bun, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sandwich hot, split the bun, and add fresh vegetables such as lettuce, tomato, or pickled onion. It pairs well with fries or a fresh side salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The sandwich is best eaten immediately. If you need to store it, wrap tightly in foil and refrigerate for up to 24 hours. Reheat in an oven or on a grill to restore the bun’s crispness.

content.title: About
content.content: The egg burrito with sausage is a hearty breakfast or snack consisting of a soft wheat tortilla filled with scrambled eggs, pieces of boiled or smoked sausage, cheese, and sometimes vegetables. The dish is popular in Mexican‑American cuisine, quick to prepare, and easy to take on the go.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico where wheat tortillas were used instead of traditional corn.
Eggs add a high‑quality protein boost, making the burrito more filling.
Sausage contributes a distinctive smoky flavor and raises the calorie count, providing a good source of quick energy for busy mornings.
In the United States the breakfast version is often called a “breakfast burrito”.
Variations may include avocado, salsa, beans or potatoes, but the basic recipe remains simple.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs and sausage together provide about 20‑25 g of protein per serving, supporting muscle repair and prolonged satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain vitamin B12, while sausage adds niacin and riboflavin, which help energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Sausage, especially beef varieties, is a good source of heme iron, important for normal blood formation.

items.title: Provides energy
items.content: Carbohydrates from the wheat tortilla give a quick glucose boost, while fats from cheese and sausage sustain energy release.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed sausage often contains a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and sausage add saturated fats, which should be limited in heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to eggs, which can cause skin reactions or more severe symptoms.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: An egg‑sausage burrito is relatively calorie‑dense (about 400‑500 kcal), so portion control is advised for weight‑management plans.

items.title: Preservatives in sausage
items.content: Certain sausages contain nitrites and other additives that may be undesirable with frequent consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The burrito is handheld and can be warmed in a microwave or on a skillet. It is often served with salsa, guacamole, or sour cream. Adding fresh veggies—tomatoes, onion, bell pepper—boosts flavor and nutrient content.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared burritos keep in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days in an airtight container. When frozen, they last up to 1 month; reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.

infant-formula-gerber-good-start-gentle-.title: Infant formula, Gerber Good Start Gentle, Stage 1, ready-to-feed

content.title: About
content.content: Gerber Good Start Gentle is a ready‑to‑feed infant formula for newborns and babies up to 6 months (Stage 1). The formula is based on partially hydrolyzed cow’s milk protein, includes prebiotic GOS and DHA, and is fortified with vitamins and minerals essential for growth and development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Designed for infants with sensitive digestion and mild protein intolerance.
Contains the prebiotic galacto‑oligosaccharides (GOS) to support healthy gut flora.
Enriched with DHA (docosahexaenoic acid) for brain and eye development.
Free from artificial colors, flavors, and preservatives.
Packaged in a sterile, ready‑to‑use pouch that can be opened without special tools.

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: Provides an optimal balance of protein, fat, and carbohydrates, along with essential vitamins (A, D, E, K) and minerals (calcium, iron, zinc) for healthy infant growth.

items.title: Brain and eye health
items.content: DHA is a key component of neuronal membranes and retinal cells, promoting cognitive and visual development.

items.title: Improved digestion
items.content: Partially hydrolyzed protein is easier to digest, and GOS prebiotic encourages growth of beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Reduced allergy risk
items.content: Hydrolyzed protein lowers the likelihood of allergic reactions in infants predisposed to food allergies.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamins C and E, together with zinc, help strengthen the infant’s immune system.

items.title: Cow’s milk allergy
items.content: Despite hydrolysis, some infants may still react to milk protein.

items.title: Improper storage
items.content: After opening, the pouch must be refrigerated and used within 48 hours to prevent spoilage.

items.title: Overheating
items.content: The formula is ready‑to‑feed; it should not be heated above 40 °C to avoid degrading sensitive nutrients.

items.title: Not for infants over 6 months
items.content: After six months, transition to a higher‑stage formula is recommended.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Since the product is ready‑to‑feed, simply open the pouch, check for integrity, and offer to the baby. If desired, gently warm to body temperature and test on the wrist before feeding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place before opening. After opening, keep refrigerated and use within 48 hours. Discard if the pouch is damaged or the formula has an off‑smell.

infant-formula-similac-isomil-soy-powder.title: Infant formula, Similac Isomil Soy, powder, made with bottled water

content.title: About
content.content: Similac Isomil Soy is a ready‑to‑feed infant formula based on soy protein, designed for babies who are lactose‑intolerant or have a cow‑milk protein sensitivity. The powder is mixed with bottled water, ensuring a consistent composition and convenient preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Developed by Abbott, a leading global manufacturer of pediatric nutrition.
Enriched with DHA and ARA, fatty acids important for brain and eye development.
Suitable for infants from birth up to 12 months who require soy‑based nutrition.
One container provides multiple daily servings when prepared according to instructions.
The formula is gluten‑free and contains no artificial colors.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Soy protein supplies all essential amino acids needed for growth and development.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Includes prebiotics and B‑vitamins that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains DHA and ARA
items.content: These long‑chain fatty acids aid neural and visual system maturation.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Soy protein is often better tolerated by infants with cow‑milk sensitivity.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Ideal for babies with lactase deficiency.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some infants may develop an allergic reaction to soy proteins.

items.title: Not a substitute for breast milk
items.content: The formula is intended as a supplement or replacement only when breastfeeding is not possible.

items.title: Correct reconstitution required
items.content: Improper water‑to‑powder ratio can lead to dehydration or over‑nutrition.

items.title: Storage after opening
items.content: Keep the opened container in a dry place and use within the stated period.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Use clean bottled water warmed to 37 °C. Add the measured amount of powder, mix thoroughly until smooth. Prepared formula should be used within 1 hour.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, use within 30 days. Do not keep prepared formula at room temperature for more than 1 hour.

content.title: About
content.content: Gatorade G is an electrolyte sports drink designed to replenish fluids and minerals lost during intense exercise. It contains sodium, potassium, magnesium, and carbohydrates that help maintain energy and speed up recovery.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gatorade was created in 1965 by researchers at the University of Southern California for the US football team.
The brand offers more than 30 flavors, and G is one of the most popular thanks to its light fruity taste.
The drink contains 6% carbohydrates, providing a quick energy boost without a sharp sugar spike.
It includes electrolytes that help prevent muscle cramps.
Gatorade G is frequently used in professional sports, including the Olympic Games.

items.title: Restores electrolyte balance
items.content: Sodium and potassium replace losses from sweat, supporting muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Supports energy levels
items.content: Carbohydrates are rapidly absorbed, providing an immediate fuel source for working muscles.

items.title: Reduces risk of dehydration
items.content: The water and electrolyte content helps re‑hydrate more quickly after intense activity.

items.title: Lessens muscle cramps
items.content: Magnesium and potassium promote normal muscle contraction and help prevent spasms.

items.title: Improves post‑workout recovery
items.content: The combination of carbs and electrolytes speeds glycogen replenishment and tissue repair.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The drink contains simple sugars, which may be undesirable for people with diabetes or those trying to lose weight.

items.title: Excess sodium
items.content: Individuals with hypertension should monitor intake, as the drink provides a notable amount of sodium.

items.title: Allergy to additives
items.content: Flavorings and colorants may cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Not a meal replacement
items.content: Gatorade is intended only for hydration and electrolyte restoration, not as a primary source of nutrients.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Consume Gatorade G before, during, and after exercise, 200–500 ml at a time. For prolonged activities, alternate with water to avoid excessive sugar intake.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, it should be consumed within 3–5 days and kept refrigerated.

content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑fat flavored tortilla chips are crisp pieces made from corn tortillas that are baked or air‑fried with less oil. They carry a light seasoning (such as cheese, barbecue, or spicy chili) and are a convenient low‑calorie snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tortilla chips originated in Mexico as a way to use leftover tortilla dough.
Reduced fat is achieved by air‑frying technology instead of deep‑frying.
Flavor blends often rely on natural spices and extracts, without artificial colors.
Corn, the base ingredient, is rich in antioxidant carotenoids.
Tortilla chips are commonly served with guacamole, salsa, or yogurt‑based dips.

items.title: Lower fat content
items.content: The reduced amount of oil makes them more suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Corn tortillas provide slowly digestible carbs that help maintain steady energy levels.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Corn fiber supports digestive health.

items.title: Provides B‑vitamins
items.content: Tortilla chips supply thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Gluten‑free when made from corn
items.content: Suitable for people with gluten intolerance if the product is certified gluten‑free.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some flavored varieties can be high in salt; choose low‑sodium options if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Rare, but a corn allergy can cause reactions.

items.title: Loss of crunch if stored improperly
items.content: Moisture can make chips soft and promote mold growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy tortilla chips as a snack on their own, with dips (salsa, guacamole, yogurt dip), or incorporate them into dishes such as chili, salads, or as a crunchy topping for casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. After opening, reseal tightly or transfer to an airtight container to maintain crispness. Discard if you notice off‑flavors or a soggy texture.
